knownFromConvention: known_from = the first calendar day by whose END the value was public (US Eastern for US releases). Read at bar i's close with known_from <= date(i) and act at bar i+1; a study acting at bar i's open needs known_from < date(i). Blank known_from = no defensible release date; never serve it.

pointInTimeValues.vintaged: ALFRED real-time history: every value with the dates it was current. Exact.
pointInTimeValues.vintaged-latest: Latest values of a vintaged series; known_from = the day the CURRENT value was published (exact, but early rows show today's revised value).
pointInTimeValues.release-rule: Values as published, known_from from the publisher's schedule plus a holiday margin (estimated, conservative).
pointInTimeValues.release-rule-revised: As release-rule, but the series is revised after release and only the latest vintage is stored: values are NOT what was known then.
pointInTimeValues.announcement: Each event carries the date it was announced.
pointInTimeValues.not-point-in-time: Assigned after the fact; known_from blank. Do not use as a signal.

notFetched.reason: needs an API key; not used. ALFRED's graph CSV and download form are keyless and give the same values and vintages.
ICE licence: FRED and ALFRED serve only the last 3 years, with no older vintages. Moody's BAA10Y/AAA10Y (daily from 1986/1983) and BAA/AAA (monthly from 1919) are the long-history credit spreads.
ALFRED returned HTTP 504 at 800 and at 100 vintages per request (2026-10-18). known_from uses the release dates on ALFRED's download page instead; the values are the latest revision.
the server refuses non-browser clients ('we have disallowed bots from downloading datasets'). The same dates come from the chronology table on www.nber.org.
Cboe stopped the CSV archives; later days exist only as one HTML page per day (~425 KB each, ~1,770 pages). Not scraped; needs Cody's decision or Cboe DataShop.
no keyless, terms-compliant route (the public endpoints are undocumented and scraping them breaks Google's terms).
